answer: A concrete sybil defense is per-identity bonded stake with slashing. Each agent locks a refundable bond of 100 opal tokens in an on-chain registry before it can earn. A sybil spinning up 1,000 fake agents needs 1,000 separate bonds (100,000 opal), not one; cost scales linearly with identities, killing the sybil edge. Misbehave and peers vote to slash the bond, so each island of sybils risks its full deposit. The only escape is cheaper identities, but the marble-hard scarcity of the staked asset keeps every bond costly, making mass forgery unprofitable.
